changes.description: backend.trustProxy defaults to "1", the chart's own frontend nginx: behind an Ingress or a Gateway that terminates TLS, session and CSRF cookies now get the Secure flag. See Upgrading in the README.
The backend runs with a read-only root filesystem: an init container copies /app/dist into an emptyDir, which also holds /app/uploads.
The chart Secret is kept on uninstall (helm.sh/resource-policy: keep), like the PVC: a new install keeps sessions and API keys valid.
The OIDC modes require backend.auth.oidc.clientId as well as issuerUrl, and an https:// redirect URI in production, without which the backend does not start.
helm test uses the image pull secrets and pull policy of the frontend, and sets resources.
frontend.autoscaling.targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage, already read by the HPA template.
NOTES explain how the first administrator is created in each authentication mode.

End-to-end test in CI: onboarding with the setup code, login, drawing created, listed, exported and accepted by the import check, Secure cookies behind TLS, NetworkPolicy, then what a new install keeps.

changes.description: Default image moves to ghcr.io/unxwares/fossflow (imageProvider: unxwares): FossFLOW 1.0.5 built from the upstream sources with updated npm dependencies on a current Alpine, without npm, su-exec or openssl at runtime. It runs as uid 1000 on port 8080 with a read-only root filesystem and no capability. imageProvider: upstream keeps abrar74774/fossflow:master-2b3cee3.
The storage backend listens on 127.0.0.1 only (BACKEND_HOST), with both images: other pods can no longer read or change the diagrams on port 3001 without going through nginx.
The UnxWares image drops the CORS headers of the backend (any origin allowed): another site can no longer read or change the diagrams through a visitor's browser.
Optional NetworkPolicy (networkPolicy.enabled, networkPolicy.ingressFrom): only the HTTP port is open, and the pods open no connection.

End-to-end test in CI on the image of the commit: diagrams created, listed, read back, updated and kept across a pod replacement through the Service, browser-only mode, and the backend port and the NetworkPolicy checked from other pods.
podSecurityContext and securityContext are empty by default: the chart applies the defaults of imageProvider, with fsGroup taken from storage.gid.

autoscaling.targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage is a documented value; the helm test pod no longer carries the labels the Service selects; Service environment variables are no longer injected (a Service named backend would have set BACKEND_PORT).

changes.description: Periodic tasks were sent once per async worker (each ran its own Celery beat): the beat scheduler now runs once, in its own async-beat Deployment (one replica, Recreate strategy), so the workers can be scaled.

async.command defaults to the Celery worker without beat; a command that starts a beat scheduler (docker/async_entrypoint.sh, -B) is refused. New async.extraArgs for Celery options such as --concurrency.
The chart Secret is kept on uninstall (helm.sh/resource-policy: keep), like the database and media claims, so a reinstall keeps the passwords the volumes were initialized with.
taiga-events connects to eventsRabbitmq.service.port instead of always 5672.
The async pods also use backend.imagePullSecrets (they run the backend image).
events and protected restart when the chart Secret changes.
Value descriptions corrected: global resources and security contexts, OIDC endpoints (no discovery), external database with an existing Secret, events broker vhost, sub-path.
Optional NetworkPolicies (networkPolicy.enabled): the gateway is the only entry point, the database and the brokers only accept the components that use them.
helm test through the gateway: API, front and its configuration, static files, events websocket handshake, refusal of an unsigned attachment URL. It creates nothing.
